tells: 1. Face close is uncanny: low-poly jaw and cheek silhouette, waxy uniform skin with no pores or specular break-up, painted-on brows, dead unfocused eyes and a mouth shape that reads as a frozen phoneme rather than a laugh (club-4-face.png, centre face)

2. A man in a grey beanie is slumped face-down on the table with his head on his arms; at TV distance it reads as passed out or broken, not laughing (club-3-mid.png, left-centre table around x 340-470, y 400-520)

3. Front-row light is flat and frontal: every front face is evenly filled at the same exposure with no rim, no candle underlight and no falloff toward the edges, so the front row looks pasted in front of a separately graded dark room (club-1-wide.png and club-6-held.png, front row x 0-1100, y 340-660)

4. Repeated gesture: three neighbours hold the same clasped-hands-at-chest pose in the same beat, which reads as a shared animation clip (club-3-mid.png, green hoodie, white blouse and grey top, x 640-1100, y 440-560; also club-2-mid.png)

5. The upper 40% of the wide is crushed black with four dead grey ceiling globes, and the back rows are grey cut-out silhouettes standing in ranks without tables, so the depth reads as a painted backdrop (club-1-wide.png, top half and back rows x 250-1000, y 280-400)
1. A flat billboard-style impostor head (a blonde face card) pokes out beside the brown-jacket woman's ear at close range, an obvious LOD pop (theatre-6-held.png, centre x 735-790, y 185-300)

2. Laugh in sync: four or five front-row faces hit the same square open-mouth shape in the same frame, and the jaw shapes are identical, so the house reads as one rig (theatre-3-mid.png, front row x 400-1060, y 330-440; theatre-6-held.png all three front faces; theatre-5-strip.png t=12.8-13.0)

3. Seat and posture mismatch: the front row sits low with knees lifted and the shins angled forward as if on a bench below the seat line; the second row looks perched or standing behind the seat backs, and isolated figures on the left side float without visible seats (theatre-1-wide.png, front row y 480-720 and left figures x 60-130, y 290-520; theatre-3-mid.png legs)

4. The face close shows faceted polygon edges on the blurred background jackets, flat waxy skin, glassy unfocused eyes and a mouth interior that is a dark slot without teeth or tongue detail (theatre-4-face.png, centre face and left jacket x 0-300)

5. The lighting cuts off hard after the first two rows: the rest of the house is a uniform blue-grey silhouette wall with three bare point lights and no aisle spill or row-by-row falloff, and the right third of each mid sits in black (theatre-1-wide.png upper 60%; theatre-2-mid.png right x 900-1280)

1. Hair cards alias badly on the face close: the fringe and the back of the head break into striped, dithered strands with hard comb lines, and they will shimmer in motion (openmic-4-face.png, top-right hair x 760-870, y 0-340)

2. The wide crowd is posed for a class photo: nearly every front-row figure sits square to the camera with arms dropped and hands on knees in the same posture, and the even frontal light makes it read as a group portrait, not a room watching a stage (openmic-1-wide.png, front row x 110-1100, y 400-720)

3. Face and laugh shapes repeat: the laughs are the same open-jaw shape tilted up, eyes stay fixed and glassy, and the green-shirt woman's head-thrown-back laugh looks at the ceiling rather than the stage (openmic-2-mid.png, x 690-1000, y 260-420)

4. Untextured geometry in the set: a flat beige slab (the door) and bare uniform walls with no practicals, posters or bounce make the room read as a grey-box level (openmic-1-wide.png, left wall x 190-250, y 250-350, and walls)

5. Contact and seam problems: the afro hair shows a visible part seam with a flat cap-like shell, and in the strip the brunette's grabbing hand intersects her neighbour's forearm (openmic-2-mid.png x 250-360, y 230-300; openmic-5-strip.png t=13.0, centre-right)
